structured_output.hypothesis: If the claim holds, no primary-freshwater fish species is native to the fresh waters of two distant continents, while many species are shared by only some river systems or countries within a single continent.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Take all FishBase species flagged as strictly freshwater (not diadromous, not euryhaline or marine-tolerant). Use only native country records (Status = native, excluding introduced, stocked, escaped or questionable records). Map countries to continents. Count species with verified native records on two or more of the distant continents Africa, South America, Australia/Oceania, Asia, and North America. Pass if, after manual checking of flagged records for taxonomic or locality errors, the verified count is 0. Also, for within-continent sharing, pass if the mean pairwise Jaccard similarity of native species lists between countries on the same continent is strictly between 0.05 and 0.95, so that species are shared but not uniformly.
structured_output.fail_criterion: Fail if one or more strictly freshwater species have verified native occurrence on two or more distant continents. Such species include Holarctic taxa like Esox lucius, if the records are native and the species is primary-freshwater. Also fail if the within-continent mean pairwise Jaccard similarity is 0.05 or lower, or 0.95 or higher.
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's 'fresh waters of distant continents' is taken as continents separated by ocean or major barriers. His 'same species' is a currently accepted valid species name in FishBase. 'Fresh-water fish' is reinterpreted as primary-freshwater fish. Diadromous and brackish species are excluded because Darwin's argument concerned dispersal that was restricted to fresh water. Introductions by humans are excluded because they were not possible dispersal routes in his sense. A 'river system' is approximated by FishBase country checklists, which are coarser than basins. Modern taxonomy may split species Darwin treated as single, so the test applies current names. A pass would show the claim holds for current species concepts. Europe and Asia are contiguous and are not counted as distant. North America and Eurasia (Holarctic) are treated as distant for the main test, and any shared species found are reported separately.

dataset.name: FishBase
dataset.why_it_fits: FishBase records species-level ecology flags (Fresh, Brack, Saltwater) and country checklists with a Status field (native, introduced, etc.). Fields used: Species, Fresh/Brack/Saltwater flags, AnaCat (migration category), Country, Status. These allow native-only, strictly freshwater species lists by country to be grouped by continent. The data are available through the web interface and the rfishbase API.
